extracted.intended_audience: lobbyists, lobbying firms, clients, in-house/outsourced compliance officers, and congressional/agency staff responsible for registration and disclosure
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and standards under the Lobbying Disclosure Act of 1995 for who must register as a lobbyist or lobbying firm, what must be reported, timing and thresholds, required contents of registrations and reports, exemptions, enforcement, and related conformity provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term "agency" has the meaning given that term in section 551(1) of title 5, United States Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Client (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term "client" means any person or entity that employs or retains another person for financial or other compensation to conduct lobbying activities on behalf of that person or entity; a person or entity whose employees act as lobbyists on its own behalf is both a client and an employer; in a coalition or association that employs or retains others to conduct lobbying, the client is the coalition or association and not its individual members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered executive branch official (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes the President, Vice President, any officer or employee in the Executive Office of the President, officers in level I–V of the Executive Schedule, members of uniformed services at pay grade O-7 or above, and any officer/employee serving in confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating positions described in 5 U.S.C. 7511(b)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered legislative branch official (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes Members of Congress, elected officers of either House, employees or individuals functioning as employees of a Member, a committee, House/Senate leadership staff, joint committees, working groups or caucuses organized to provide legislative services or assistance to Members, and other legislative branch employees as described under section 109(13) of the Ethics in Government Act of 1978 (5 U.S.C. App.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee (definition; exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term "employee" means any individual who is an officer, employee, partner, director, or proprietor of a person or entity, but does not include independent contractors or volunteers who receive no financial or other compensation from the person or entity for their services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign entity (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term "foreign entity" means a foreign principal as defined in section 1(b) of the Foreign Agents Registration Act of 1938 (22 U.S.C. 611(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lobbying activities (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term "lobbying activities" means lobbying contacts and efforts in support of such contacts, including preparation and planning activities, research and other background work that is intended, at the time it is performed, for use in contacts, and coordination with the lobbying activities of others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lobbying contact (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term "lobbying contact" means any oral or written communication (including an electronic communication) to a covered executive branch official or a covered legislative branch official that is made on behalf of a client with regard to: (i) formulation/modification/adoption of Federal legislation (including legislative proposals); (ii) formulation/modification/adoption of a Federal rule, regulation, Executive order, or other program/policy/position of the U.S. Government; (iii) administration or execution of a Federal program or policy (including negotiation, award, administration of a Federal contract, grant, loan, permit, or license); or (iv) nomination or confirmation of a person for a Senate-confirmed position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes electronic communications. The statute also enumerates many exceptions (see next entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lobbying contact exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications that are not considered "lobbying contacts" include: (i) made by a public official in official capacity; (ii) by a media representative for news-gathering/dissemination; (iii) in a speech/article/public material distributed to the public or through mass media; (iv) on behalf of a foreign government/party disclosed under FARA; (v) a request for a meeting/status if it does not include an attempt to influence; (vi) in participation on a Federal Advisory Committee; (vii) testimony before or submitted to Congressional committee for public record; (viii) information provided in writing in response to an official request for specific information; (ix) required by subpoena or compelled by statute/regulation; (x) in response to notices in the Federal Register or similar solicitations directed to the designated official; (xi) communications not reportable without disclosing prohibited information; (xii) made to an agency official regarding judicial, law enforcement, or otherwise confidential proceedings where agency is charged with responsibility; (xiii) made in compliance with written agency procedures for adjudications under 5 U.S.C. 554; (xiv) written comments filed in public proceedings or on-the-record communications; (xv) petitions for agency action required to be public record; (xvi) communications on behalf of an individual regarding that individual's benefits/employment/personal matters (with specified exceptions for private legislation); (xvii) protected whistleblower disclosures; (xviii) made by certain churches or religious orders exempt from filing Federal income tax returns; and (xix) communications between officials of specified self-regulatory organizations and the SEC/CFTC concerning regulatory responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These exceptions narrow what counts as a reportable lobbying contact; practitioners must evaluate communications against this detailed list before assuming reporting is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lobbying firm (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term "lobbying firm" means a person or entity that has one or more employees who are lobbyists on behalf of a client other than that person or entity; includes a self-employed individual who is a lobbyist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lobbyist (definition and threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term "lobbyist" means any individual who is employed or retained by a client for financial or other compensation for services that include more than one lobbying contact, other than an individual whose lobbying activities constitute less than 20 percent of the time engaged in the services provided by such individual to that client over a six month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines who must register as a lobbyist; includes both frequency (more than one contact) and time-share threshold (20% over six months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Media organization (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term "media organization" means a person or entity engaged in disseminating information to the general public through newspaper, magazine, other publication, radio, television, cable, or other mass communication medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration timing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than 45 days after a lobbyist first makes a lobbying contact or is employed or retained to make a lobbying contact, whichever is earlier, such lobbyist (or the organization employing such lobbyist) shall register with the Secretary of the Senate and the Clerk of the House of Representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to individuals who meet the "lobbyist" definition and to organizations per employer-filing rules; calendar/act-in-good-faith timing compliance is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer filing for organizations with lobbyists
rubrics_metrics.description: Any organization that has one or more employees who are lobbyists shall file a single registration on behalf of such employees for each client on whose behalf the employees act as lobbyists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregates employee lobbyist reporting under the organization's registration rather than requiring each employee to register separately for that client.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration exemptions and monetary thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: A person or entity is not required to register if: (i) for a lobbying firm, total income for matters related to lobbying activities on behalf of a particular client does not exceed and is not expected to exceed $5,000; or (ii) for an organization whose employees lobby on its own behalf, total expenses in connection with lobbying activities do not exceed or are not expected to exceed $20,000 in the semiannual period (as estimated under section 5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Threshold amounts are subject to periodic CPI adjustment (first on Jan 1, 1997 and every fourth year thereafter), rounded to nearest $500. Exemptions are per-client and per-semiannual period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Each registration shall contain: (1) name, address, business telephone, principal place of business of the registrant, and a general description of its business/activities; (2) name, address, principal place of business of the registrant's client and general description of client's business/activities (if different); (3) name/address/principal place/business of any organization (other than the client) that contributes more than $10,000 toward the registrant's lobbying activities in a semiannual period and that in whole or in major part plans, supervises, or controls such lobbying activities; (4) for any foreign entity that (A) holds at least 20% equitable ownership in the client or organization in (3), (B) directly/indirectly plans/supervises/controls/finances/subsidizes the client's activities, or (C) is an affiliate with direct interest in outcome: name/address/principal place/business, amount of any contribution > $10,000 to lobbying activities, and approximate percentage of equitable ownership in the client; (5) a statement of general issue areas registrant expects to engage in on behalf of client and, to extent practicable, specific issues already addressed or likely to be addressed as of registration date; (6) the name of each employee who has acted or is expected to act as a lobbyist for the client and, if any such employee served as a covered executive or legislative branch official in the prior 2 years before first acting as a lobbyist for the client, the position in which such employee served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration must be client-specific and disclose financial contributors, foreign ties, issue areas, and personnel with recent government service. Provide as much specificity as practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for multiple clients and multiple contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant makes lobbying contacts on behalf of more than one client, a separate registration shall be filed for each client. A registrant who makes more than one lobbying contact for the same client shall file a single registration covering all such contacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration is per-client; avoid duplicative filings for multiple contacts with same client but file separately per client.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of registration
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant who after registration is no longer employed or retained by a client to conduct lobbying activities, and does not anticipate any additional lobbying activities for that client, may notify the Secretary of the Senate and the Clerk of the House of Representatives and terminate its registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows de-registration when representation ceases and no future lobbying is anticipated; requires affirmative notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semiannual reporting timing
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than 45 days after the end of the semiannual period beginning on the first day of each January and the first day of July in each year in which a registrant is registered under section 4, each registrant shall file a report on its lobbying activities during that semiannual period. A separate report shall be filed for each client of the registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports are strictly calendar semiannual and client-specific; plan for recurring reporting deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of semiannual report
rubrics_metrics.description: Each semiannual report shall contain: (1) the name of the registrant, the name of the client, and any changes/updates to registration information; (2) for each general issue area in which the registrant engaged in lobbying during the period: (A) a list of specific issues on which a lobbyist engaged in lobbying activities, including to the maximum extent practicable bill numbers and references to specific executive branch actions; (B) a statement of the Houses of Congress and Federal agencies contacted by lobbyists employed by the registrant on behalf of the client; (C) a list of employees of the registrant who acted as lobbyists on behalf of the client; (D) a description of any interest of any foreign entity identified under section 4(b)(4) in the specific issues listed; (3) for a lobbying firm, a good faith estimate of total amount of all income from the client during the semiannual period (excluding income unrelated to lobbying); (4) for a registrant lobbying on its own behalf, a good faith estimate of total expenses incurred in connection with lobbying activities during the semiannual period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports must be as specific as practicable (bill numbers, agencies contacted, personnel); income/expense estimates are required by registrant type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimates of income or expenses (rounding and small amounts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimates in excess of $10,000 shall be rounded to the nearest $20,000. If income or expenses do not exceed $10,000, the registrant shall include a statement that income or expenses totaled less than $10,000 for the reporting period. A registrant that reports lobbying expenditures pursuant to 26 U.S.C. 6033(b)(8) may satisfy the requirement to report income or expenses by filing a copy of the form filed under that Code section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the statutory rounding rules for public filings; small amounts have a special 'less than $10,000' disclosure rather than precise numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure and enforcement duties of Secretary/Clerk
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of the Senate and the Clerk of the House shall: (1) provide guidance and assistance on registration and reporting requirements and develop common standards, rules, and procedures for compliance; (2) review, verify, and inquire as necessary to ensure accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of registrations and reports; (3) develop filing, coding, and cross-indexing systems (including a public list of registered lobbyists, firms, and clients and computerized systems to minimize burden/maximize public access); (4) make registrations and reports available for public inspection and copying at reasonable times; (5) retain registrations for at least 6 years after termination and reports for at least 6 years after filing; (6) compile and summarize information for each semiannual period clearly and completely; (7) notify any lobbyist or lobbying firm in writing that may be in noncompliance; (8) notify the U.S. Attorney for D.C. that a lobbyist or firm may be in noncompliance if the registrant has been notified in writing and has failed to provide an appropriate response within 60 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes administrative and enforcement responsibilities including public access, record retention, compliance notices, and referral to prosecutors after failed responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for knowing violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Whoever knowingly fails to (1) remedy a defective filing within 60 days after notice of such defect by the Secretary or Clerk, or (2) comply with any other provision of this Act; shall, upon proof of such knowing violation by a preponderance of the evidence, be subject to a civil fine of not more than $50,000, depending on the extent and gravity of the violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civil fines are conditioned on a showing of knowing violation and the penalty amount is discretionary up to statutory maximum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules of construction protecting constitutional rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this Act shall be construed to prohibit or interfere with (1) the right to petition the Government for redress of grievances; (2) the right to express a personal opinion; or (3) the right of association protected by the First Amendment. Nothing shall be construed to prohibit lobbying activities regardless of compliance status, and nothing grants general audit or investigative authority to the Secretary/Clerk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory requirements are subject to these express constitutional and scope-preserving constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to FARA and related conformity provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act amends the Foreign Agents Registration Act (FARA) to revise language (e.g., replace 'political propaganda' with 'informational materials'), add agents required to register under the LDA to FARA where appropriate, define conspicuous statement rules for informational materials distributed by agents of foreign principals, and other conforming edits to FARA provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign representation and disclosures must be reconciled with both LDA and FARA obligations; practitioners should consult both statutes for cross-cutting duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification at time of oral lobbying contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person or entity that makes an oral lobbying contact with a covered official shall, on the request of the official at the time of the contact: (1) state whether the person or entity is registered under this Act and identify the client on whose behalf the contact is made; and (2) state whether such client is a foreign entity and identify any foreign entity required to be disclosed under section 4(b)(4) that has a direct interest in the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate on-request oral disclosures are required during face-to-face or telephone lobbying contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification for written lobbying contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Any registrant who makes a written lobbying contact (including electronic communication) shall: (1) if the client is a foreign entity, identify such client, state that the client is considered a foreign entity under this Act, and state whether the person making the contact is registered on behalf of that client under section 4; and (2) identify any other foreign entity identified under section 4(b)(4) that has a direct interest in the outcome of the lobbying activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written and electronic communications have specific mandatory disclosure content regarding foreign clients and registration status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification as covered official upon request
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon request by a person or entity making a lobbying contact, the individual who is contacted or the office employing that individual shall indicate whether or not the individual is a covered legislative branch official or a covered executive branch official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps lobbyists confirm whether a contacted person is within the statute's covered official definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimates based on tax reporting (permitted alternative procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant required to report lobbying expenditures under 26 U.S.C. 6033(b)(8) or subject to 26 U.S.C. 162(e) may: (a) make a good faith estimate by category of dollar value of amounts required to be disclosed under sections 4(a)(3) and 5(b)(4) and, in lieu of the LDA definition of 'lobbying activities', consider as lobbying activities only those influencing legislation as defined in 26 U.S.C. 4911(d) (for 6033 filers); or (b) make good faith estimates of amounts not deductible under 162(e) and, in lieu of the LDA definition, consider as lobbying activities only those costs not deductible under 162(e). A registrant electing these procedures must inform the Secretary/Clerk that it has elected them and make all such estimates in a given calendar year under those procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an alternative, tax-code-aligned method of estimating/reporting for organizations already filing certain IRS forms; election must be consistent across the calendar year and communicated to the Clerk/Secretary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller General study requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Not later than March 31, 1997, the Comptroller General shall review reporting by registrants under the tax-based estimate procedures and report to Congress differences between the LDA definition of 'lobbying activities' and related tax-code definitions, the impact on filing/reporting, and any recommended changes to harmonize definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical requirement to study harmonization; signals potential future statutory/regulatory alignment but not itself a filing requirement for registrants now.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeals and conforming amendments to other statutes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act repeals the Federal Regulation of Lobbying Act (2 U.S.C. 261 et seq.) and certain HUD/housing lobbying provisions, and makes conforming amendments to numerous statutes (e.g., Title 18, Foreign Service Act, Competitiveness Policy Council Act) to incorporate or reference LDA definitions such as 'lobbyist' and 'foreign entity'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners should be aware that LDA replaced earlier statutory frameworks and that other statutes were amended to reflect LDA definitions/requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exempt organizations and federal funds prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: An organization described in section 501(c)(4) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 which engages in lobbying activities shall not be eligible for the receipt of Federal funds constituting an award, grant, contract, loan, or any other form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 501(c)(4) groups that lobby foreclose eligibility for federal awards/grants/contracts/loans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial disclosure amendments (Ethics in Government Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments require more granular dollar categories for income and assets on Ethics in Government Act filings (e.g., new brackets: > $1,000,000 but ≤ $5,000,000, > $5,000,000, and expanded asset/liability brackets up to > $50,000,000) and provide rules on when spouse/dependent holdings are attributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alters thresholds and categories for public financial disclosures of certain officials; relevant to officials with lobbying-related financial interests or subsequent employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ban on certain Trade Representative post-service representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments prohibit the United States Trade Representative and Deputy United States Trade Representative from representing or advising foreign entities after service (inserting 'or Deputy United States Trade Representative' and striking the prior 3-year limitation to make the restriction apply 'at any time'); also prohibits appointment as U.S. Trade Representative/Deputy for individuals who directly represented/advised a foreign entity in trade negotiations or disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Places lifetime restrictions on certain high-level Trade Representative roles concerning representation of foreign entities; relevant to former lobbyists seeking such appointments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates and transition rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise provided, the Act and amendments take effect January 1, 1996. Repeals and amendments shall not affect proceedings or suits commenced before the effective date, and agencies' requirements to compile, publish, and retain information filed or received before the effective date remain in effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when statutory obligations became operative and preserves pre-effective-date proceedings and records obligations.
